text.text: Everything the agency runs on, in one place: clients and their retainers, campaigns, the deliverables inside them, time logged and the monthly reports owed. Start with the Dashboard each Monday, then work the Overdue and Mine views. Check Hours used on every client before agreeing extra work.
Clients
The brands the agency runs programs for, with their retainer terms.
Campaigns
Each program the agency runs for a client.
Deliverables
The pieces of work inside a campaign, from ad sets to landing pages.
Time entries
Hours logged against clients and campaigns, the source of every retainer figure.
Monthly reports
The report owed to each client every month.
The agency at a glance. Charts read from the live tables, so they move as the team logs time and updates statuses.
Deliverables overdue
Reports waiting on us
Renewing in the next 30 days
How to read the numbers

cells.text: Hours logged this month divided by the hours included in the retainer
At 80 percent warn the client; at 100 percent agree extra hours or scope in writing
Renewal date minus today; negative means the renewal date has passed
Book the review call at 45 days; chase any negative number today
Spend to date divided by the ad budget
Over 100 means overspend; under 60 near the end means underspend
Deliverables done divided by deliverables in the campaign
Below plan at the halfway date means re-plan with the client

text.text: A report is what keeps a retainer renewed. Clients rarely remember the work, they remember the story you told about it.
When it happens
Start on the second working day of the month, once ad platforms have settled their final numbers.
Every report row in the Monthly reports table is due by the fifth working day. Drafting beyond that needs the account manager to tell the client.
Build it in five steps
Open the client row and read Hours used this month and Campaigns live.
Pull the spend and result figures from each channel into the report row's Numbers section.
Write the headline last. It should say what changed and why in one sentence.
List what shipped from the Deliverables table, using the Done filter for that client.
Write the recommendation: one thing to start, one to stop, one decision you need from them.
Before you send
Numbers match the platform screens, not last month's copy
Hours used is shown against hours included
Every recommendation names who decides and by when
A second person read the headline
After sending
Press Mark sent on the report row so the client's Reports owed count drops, then log any follow-up questions as deliverables.
The first thirty days decide whether a client sees you as a vendor or a partner. Treat access as the first deliverable.
Week one
Contract and retainer terms entered on the client row (fee, hours included, renewal date)
Kickoff call held; notes saved in the client page
Access requested: ad accounts, analytics, tag manager, email platform, CMS
Shared folder created and the client contact told where assets go
First campaign row created with a goal that has a number in it
Weeks two and three
Audit the tracking before spending money: do conversions fire once, with the right value?
Agree the reporting day and who receives the report.
Set the weekly call and put the standing agenda in the client page.
Week four
Send a short first-month note: what was learned, what is planned, what is needed from them.
Review hours used against hours included and tell the client if the scope looks too small or too large.
Common traps
Accepting access to a personal account instead of the business account.
Starting ads before conversion tracking is checked.
Promising a result date before you have seen thirty days of data.
Hours are the agency's only stock. These rules keep the balance honest without making clients feel metered.
Logging time
Log time the same day. Use one entry per client per task, with the campaign filled in when there is one.
Internal work such as pitches and training is not billable; untick Billable.
Reading the numbers

cells.text: Tell the client this week which work will finish first
Agree extra hours or drop scope before doing more

text.text: Handling extra requests
Write down the request in the client page with a rough hour estimate.
Offer two options: swap it for planned work, or buy extra hours.
Record the decision and log the work against the right campaign.
At renewal
Open the renewal view at 45 days. Bring last quarter's results, hours used per month and one proposal to grow the scope.
Monday
Open the Dashboard and read the overdue deliverables list aloud. Each item gets an owner and a new date or a reason.
Check Reports waiting on us and assign authors.
Midweek
Account managers review Hours used on their clients and flag anything near the limit.
Paid media checks pacing: Budget spent against days elapsed.
Friday
Everyone logs the week's time before leaving.
Move finished deliverables to Done so campaign progress is true.
Write one line per live campaign in its page: what happened and what is next.
A Friday that ends with clean statuses makes Monday a ten minute meeting.
